Gboard Next-Word Prediction and Smart Suggestions Flags

A practical guide to next-word prediction, multiword suggestions, user-history signals and inline suggestion experiments.

What you should know

NWP and inline suggestions are different stages of suggesting text, and neither should be confused with autocorrection.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Prediction is not a single feature

Gboard may surface next-word predictions, multiword completions, inline suggestions or context-dependent chips. Their signals can include the typed prefix, language, earlier context and on-device history. Flags such as enable_nwp_tflite_engine refer to implementation choices, not a universal option that increases intelligence.

Look at the presentation layer too

enable_inline_suggestions_on_decoder_side and enable_inline_suggestions_on_client_side imply separate processing points. If a result appears in one text field and not another, the receiving application may matter. Treat a UI hint as different evidence from changes in model quality or speed.

Compare useful examples

Type a familiar three-word prefix, repeat it in multiple apps and record whether suggestions appear, how many words they span and whether tapping them inserts exactly the expected text. Repeat after any change using the same locale, model state and connectivity. Resist the temptation to change both a model flag and a suggestion-strip flag together.

Frequently asked questions

Why do suggestions vary between apps?

Different text-field capabilities and app integration can influence the UI, even when the same keyboard is active.

Is NWP the same as autocorrect?

No. Next-word prediction offers future text; autocorrection revises or replaces what you typed.
